terms.definition: A tiny pore on the surface of a leaf or stem that opens and closes to allow gases to pass.
terms.function: Lets carbon dioxide in and oxygen out.
terms.whereItIs: On the outer surface of leaves and stems.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the main doorway for the gases a plant needs for life.

terms.definition: One of two cells beside a stoma that swell to open the pore and relax to close it.
terms.function: Controls whether the stoma is open or closed.
terms.whereItIs: Framing each stomata pore on the leaf.
terms.whyItMatters: It lets the plant decide when to exchange gas and when to save water.

terms.definition: The movement of carbon dioxide into a leaf and oxygen out through the stomata.
terms.function: Brings in a plant's food-making gas and removes the oxygen it makes.
terms.whereItIs: Through the open stomata on the leaf.
terms.whyItMatters: It is how plants take in what they need make food.

terms.definition: The loss of water vapor from a plant through its stomata.
terms.function: A side effect of open stomata that the plant keeps under control by closing the pores to save water.
terms.whereItIs: Mainly through the stomata on the leaves.
terms.whyItMatters: It links the constancy of breathing to the plant's need to conserve water.
